metadata.case_name: WONG SUN CHEONG, SUING BY HIS NEXT FRIEND LEE YIN SHEUNG v. CHOI CHI KONG AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: delivery man at Kai Ming Food Shop

injuries.source: P sustained severe head injuries as is borne out by the agreed medical evidence.

injuries.description: Fractures on the left side of his skull
injuries.source: Radiological investigations showed fractures on the left side of his skull
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of skull or facial bones, part unspecified
Traumatic subdural haemorrhage, unspecified whether acute or chronic

injuries.source: Radiological investigations showed ... contusion of the brain substance.

In August 2012, while having lunch at home, he developed status epilepticus with refractory generalized epileptic seizures. ... he was then started on the antiepileptic drug phenytoin which he continues to take.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

injuries.description: Skull defect following craniectomy (required cranioplasty with metallic prosthesis)
injuries.source: Emergency operation was done that day to evacuate blood clots and to insert a ventricular drain. ... In May 2012, he was re-admitted to QEH for his third operation, a cranioplasty to repair the skull defect with a metallic prosthesis.

manifestations.description: Prolonged post-traumatic amnesia (estimated as over one month)
Cognitive dysfunction (MMSE 18/30; mild to moderate dementia)
Epilepsy / generalized epileptic seizures (controlled with phenytoin; seizure-free since August 2012 episode)
Impaired ability to express himself (often using the wrong words)
Impaired balance / truncal ataxia; walked stably but could not walk heel to toe
Right leg mild spasticity with heightened reflexes
Not employable in any capacity (permanent loss of earning capacity 100%)
Not capable of managing his own legal and financial affairs; not fully independent even inside the home

treatments_received: Emergency operation to evacuate blood clots
Second emergency operation to evacuate more blood clots
Cranioplasty to repair skull defect with a metallic prosthesis
Intubation and care in the intensive care unit
Rehabilitation (transfer to Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation)
treatments_future: Lifelong care and attention (cost of hiring a domestic helper was claimed)

losses.description: Severe head injury with skull fractures, subarachnoid bleeding, subdural bleeding and contusion of the brain substance requiring emergency neurosurgery.
Cognitive dysfunction; MMSE 18/30 giving mild to moderate dementia; slowed comprehension.
Dysphasia: naming difficulty, impaired ability to express himself and impaired understanding of verbal communications.
Not capable of managing his own legal and financial affairs and not fully independent even inside the home; needs care and attention for the rest of his life.
Walked stably but could not walk heel to toe and showed truncal ataxia; impaired balance.
Not employable in any capacity; permanent loss of earning capacity was 100%.

comparable_cases.case_name: Cheung Wai Ping v Chan Yuen Yee
Chan Sze Ki v Department of Justice & another

evidence: as a result of the severe head injury P had dysphasia (problem with language) and cognitive dysfunction and epilepsy.
as a result of the severe head injury P had dysphasia (problem with language) and cognitive dysfunction and epilepsy.
He scored 18 points out of a possible 30 on the mini mental state examination. This put him into the category of mild to moderate dementia.
They were of the view that P is not capable of managing his own legal and financial affairs and is not fully independent even inside the home.
It was accepted that P needs care and attention for the rest of his life with his life expectancy at 80 years.
He walked stably but could not walk heel to toe, showing truncal ataxia.
They were of the view that P is not employable in any capacity. His permanent loss of earning capacity was 100%.

injury_loss_relations.injury: Fractures on the left side of his skull; intracranial bleeding; brain contusion
evidence: Radiological investigations showed fractures on the left side of his skull, subarachnoid bleeding, subdural bleeding as well as contusion of the brain substance.
